senses.sense_definition: The transmission or spread of a disease from one person or organism to another by direct or indirect contact.

examples.text: Frequent handwashing is essential to reduce the risk of <w>contagion</w> during flu season.
Health officials took strict measures to prevent the <w>contagion</w> from spreading to nearby towns.

senses.sense_definition: A contagious disease, or the harmful agent that transmits it.

examples.text: The entire village was quarantined after a deadly <w>contagion</w> began spreading among the livestock.
Scientists rushed to develop a vaccine against the novel <w>contagion</w>.

senses.sense_definition: The rapid spread of an idea, emotion, or behavior among people in a group or community.

examples.text: A sudden <w>contagion</w> of panic swept through the crowd when the alarm sounded.
Her cheerful laughter created a delightful <w>contagion</w> that brightened the entire room.

senses.sense_definition: The transmission of financial distress, shocks, or economic instability across different markets or countries.

examples.text: Central banks intervened quickly to avoid financial <w>contagion</w> across global markets.
The collapse of a major bank triggered severe <w>contagion</w> throughout the regional economy.

senses.sense_definition: An economic crisis or recession that has developed as a result of cross-market spillover effects.

examples.text: Policy makers struggled to contain the regional <w>contagion</w> before it ruined international trade.
The current economic <w>contagion</w> originated from the sudden collapse of property values abroad.
